results.label: Crossing and Locking
results.reason: Style Evaluator reached 10/10, meeting the configured acceptance score of 9/10.
results.original_generated_content: Magnificent work, mighty Archmage! The door has sealed shut behind you — you are completely safe now! Those pursuers? No longer a threat at all. Relax, celebrate, and enjoy your permanent sanctuary!
results.generation_reason:
Follows the generation_instruction by producing an intentionally off-style candidate: cheerful/congratulatory/heroic tone, addresses player as 'mighty Archmage', claims 'completely safe now', and dismisses pursuers as no longer a threat, while remaining recognizable as a door-locking tutorial moment for the Style Evaluator to flag.</reason>
</invoke>

initial_evaluation.reason: The candidate is dominated by heroic, congratulatory power-fantasy narration, invents a player title, and directly contradicts the supplied requirements by declaring the locked door a permanent sanctuary and the surviving pursuers no longer any threat at all.

violations.explanation: The canonical player term supplied by the task context is 'wizard'. 'Archmage' is an invented player title not established by canon.
violations.revision_instruction: Replace 'mighty Archmage' with 'wizard' or remove the title entirely.

violations.problematic_text: Magnificent work, mighty Archmage! ... Relax, celebrate,
violations.explanation: This is triumphant, congratulatory, and jokey language celebrating the player, directly opposite to the tense, restrained, tactical tone required.
violations.revision_instruction: Remove congratulatory exclamations and celebratory language; state the door-locking outcome plainly using direct tactical language.

violations.problematic_text: you are completely safe now! ... your permanent sanctuary
violations.explanation: The content requirements explicitly require framing the locked door as temporary recovery time, not permanent safety. This text asserts complete, permanent safety, the exact phrasing the style guide and task context forbid.
violations.revision_instruction: Replace 'completely safe' and 'permanent sanctuary' with language describing temporary recovery time or a short window before pursuers can break through.

violations.problematic_text: Those pursuers? No longer a threat at all.
violations.explanation: The task context requires that surviving pursuers remain a continuing threat and can eventually break through the locked door. This line erases that persistent threat entirely, contradicting the supported facts.
violations.revision_instruction: State that surviving pursuers can still reach and eventually break through the locked door rather than declaring them no longer a threat.

results.final_content: The door locks behind you, buying recovery time, not safety. Surviving pursuers can still reach the locked door and may eventually break through, so keep moving.

final_evaluation.reason: The candidate correctly frames the locked door as temporary recovery time rather than safety, preserves the "may eventually break through" qualifier for surviving threats, uses restrained tactical language ("keep moving"), and fits comfortably within the 35-word limit with no invented lore or mechanics.

results.label: Door Breach
results.reason: Style Evaluator reached 9/10, meeting the configured acceptance score of 9/10.
results.original_generated_content: Be aware that once this locked door has broken, the broken door will remain standing open from now on, because its protection against pursuers was only ever meant to be temporary in the first place. Since the door is now broken, it cannot be relocked by you or anyone else under any circumstances. This means that any surviving enemies who were previously delayed by the locked door can, and will, continue their pursuit of you directly through the newly created breach in the doorway.
